clue.text: Seabirds or seabird coming west

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming west means the word runs right to left, so it is read backwards

parts.note: a skua is a predatory seabird

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher's note: a flock of seabirds, or maybe a single one, flying in from the west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming west' turns SKUA round to give the plural bird names.
explanation.definitionFit: Auks are diving seabirds of northern seas, such as puffins and guillemots.

clue.text: Statement FIFA put out: US lawyer against it

indicators.note: put out suggests the letters are disturbed or knocked out of place, so they are rearranged

parts.note: a DA is a District Attorney, a US prosecutor
V is short for versus, meaning against
taken as written

explanation.surface: Football's governing body issues a statement, and an American lawyer opposes it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' rearranges FIFA into AFFI.
explanation.definitionFit: An affidavit is a written statement sworn on oath for use as evidence in court.

clue.text: Revolutionary drink sweetheart uncovered

parts.note: kir is a French aperitif of white wine and blackcurrant liqueur

indicators.note: uncovered says the word for sweetheart loses its outer letters, its covering

parts.note: love is a term of endearment for a sweetheart

explanation.surface: A revolutionary sips a drink while his sweetheart appears without her clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncovered' strips L and E from LOVE, leaving OV.
explanation.definitionFit: Sergei Kirov was a Bolshevik leader of the Russian Revolution whose assassination in 1934 sparked Stalin's purges.

clue.text: Eastern film director walked around to guillotine

indicators.note: around tells us to turn the whole string of pieces round so it reads backwards

parts.note: Jacques Tati was a French film director, maker of Monsieur Hulot's Holiday
paced means walked, step by step

explanation.surface: An Eastern film director strolled around before an execution by guillotine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' reverses ETATIPACED as a whole, giving DECAP-ITAT-E.
explanation.definitionFit: A guillotine beheads its victim, so to guillotine someone is to cut off their head.

clue.text: Poet remains active when book released

indicators.note: released says the letter for book is let go from the words before it

parts.note: embers are the glowing remains of a fire
on means working or active, as a machine switched on

explanation.surface: A poet's legacy stays alive once his book is published.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when book released' takes B out of EMBERSON.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph Waldo Emerson was a nineteenth-century American essayist and poet of Transcendentalism.

clue.text: Preacher throws stone into a bar

indicators.note: throws describes putting the stone abbreviation forcibly into something
into says where the stone abbreviation goes, inside the word for bar

parts.note: a pole is a long bar
st is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight

explanation.surface: An angry preacher hurls a stone through a pub window.
explanation.walkthrough: ST is the stone, the British unit of body weight; 'bar' is a pole, not a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostles were the disciples sent out by Jesus to spread his teaching, preachers of the gospel.

clue.text: Bright bunch working for TV hearing news as it breaks

indicators.note: hearing tells us the phrase for working in television is taken by its sound

parts.note: someone working for TV is in telly, telly being British slang for television
gen is British slang for information or news

indicators.note: breaks says the words as it are smashed up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A clever team of TV journalists listening to breaking news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks' rearranges AS IT into TSIA.
explanation.definitionFit: The intelligentsia are the intellectual class, a group of clever, educated people.

clue.text: Dolorous one in Scots area — he had to go under

indicators.note: in a down clue, to go under means this piece is placed below, after the rest
in says the numeral sits inside the Scottish area

parts.note: Angus is a council area of eastern Scotland
I is the Roman numeral for one
he'd is the contraction of he had

explanation.surface: A grieving man in a Scottish region who had gone under, as if drowned or bankrupt.
explanation.walkthrough: Angus is a council area of eastern Scotland; 'to go under' places the last piece below in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolorous is a literary word for full of grief or sorrow, as an anguished person is.

clue.text: Man from drive-in restaurant turned up

indicators.note: turned up says the hidden letters are read backwards
from says the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A man spotted at a drive-in diner, having just arrived there.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft lacked an indicator for the hidden run; 'from' supplies it. In a down clue 'turned up' reads the run upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernie is a man's name, a familiar form of Ernest.

clue.text: Celestial phenomenon stars follow and not sailors

indicators.note: follow says the word for stars comes after the rest in the answer

parts.note: nor means and not
the RN, the Royal Navy, stands for sailors
stars are lights in the sky

explanation.surface: A sky-watcher's note on stars that guide, not for sailors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sailors' gives THE RN, the Royal Navy, article included; 'follow' places the stars last.
explanation.definitionFit: The aurora borealis is a shimmering display of coloured light in the far northern night sky.

clue.text: Given up working in smithy

indicators.note: in says the word for working goes inside the word for smithy

parts.note: a forge is a blacksmith's workshop
on means working, as a machine switched on

explanation.surface: Someone has quit their job at a blacksmith's workshop.
explanation.definitionFit: Forgone is the past participle of forgo, meaning done without or relinquished.

clue.text: Figure provided in month before November

parts.note: Oct is the short form of October
ago means before, in the past
November is N in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A number supplied for the month leading up to November.
explanation.definitionFit: An octagon is an eight-sided plane shape, a geometric figure.

clue.text: Cover verse in song for two

indicators.note: in says the letter for verse goes inside the song

parts.note: a duet is a piece for two performers

explanation.surface: A singer covers a verse within a duet.
explanation.definitionFit: A duvet is a quilted bed covering filled with down or synthetic fibre.

clue.text: Body going round worried student pair entering place

indicators.note: entering says these letters go inside the word for place

parts.note: a site is a place or location
ate means worried, as in what's eating you

indicators.note: pair says the learner letter is taken twice

parts.note: L is for learner, a student driver's L-plate

explanation.surface: An anxious couple of students arriving somewhere while someone circles.
explanation.walkthrough: ATE is the past tense of eat, as in 'what's eating you?'.
explanation.definitionFit: A satellite is a moon or spacecraft that orbits a planet, a body circling another.

clue.text: Retribution from Gene after bashing in lead at church

indicators.note: in says the rearranged name goes inside the word for lead

parts.note: the van, or vanguard, is the lead position

indicators.note: after bashing means the name Gene is battered into a new order

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A man named Gene gets revenge after a fight that started at church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after bashing' is the anagram signal for Gene, not a time word; 'lead' is the van, the front position.
explanation.definitionFit: Vengeance is punishment inflicted in return for a wrong, the same as retribution.

clue.text: Go on, smile — that's rude new word

indicators.note: rude in the sense of crude or roughly made, so the letters are roughly rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone urging a friend to grin at a word that is a bit crude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rude' rearranges GOONSMILE.
explanation.definitionFit: A neologism is a newly coined word or expression.

clue.text: Limitlessly rich ore that filled ancient vessels

indicators.note: limitlessly says the two words lose their limits, the outer letters, leaving a run inside them

explanation.surface: An endlessly rich ore that once filled ancient ships or urns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessels' looks like ships or pots; it means the veins of the Greek gods.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth ichor was the ethereal fluid flowing in the gods' veins instead of blood.

clue.text: Hope land has game girl raised in America

parts.note: RU is rugby union
Rita is a girl's name

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the short word is turned upwards, reading backwards

explanation.surface: A girl brought up in America has a game hoping to reach the promised land.
explanation.walkthrough: Anthony Hope is the author meant here; 'Hope' is no wish.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruritania is the fictional Central European kingdom in Anthony Hope's novel The Prisoner of Zenda.

clue.text: Old character is prickly sort

definitions.meaning: the Old English letter þ, used for the th sound
a sharp spine on a plant, or a person who is a constant irritation

explanation.surface: An elderly eccentric who is touchy and difficult.
explanation.definitionFit: Thorn was a runic letter of Old English, and also a sharp spike on a rose stem.

clue.text: One has aspirations before the contract bid

parts.note: pre is a prefix meaning before
a tender is a formal offer to carry out work under contract

explanation.surface: An ambitious company submitting its bid before the contract is awarded.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretender claims a throne or title, aspiring to it, as Bonnie Prince Charlie the Young Pretender did.

clue.text: Rapper revised English in draft

indicators.note: in says the letter for English goes inside the rearranged letters
revised suggests a reworking, so the letters of rapper are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rapper revises the English in his first draft of lyrics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised' rearranges RAPPER, and E goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To draft a document is to draw it up, to make it ready in preliminary form.

clue.text: Muse quiet in tree swaying at country club?

parts.note: the EU, the European Union, is a club of countries

indicators.note: in says the letter for quiet sits inside the rearranged letters
swaying suggests the tree moves about, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A quiet moment beneath a swaying tree at a golf country club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'country club' is not a golf club but the European Union, a club of countries; 'swaying' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Euterpe is the Greek Muse of music and lyric poetry, one of the nine daughters of Zeus.

clue.text: Outstanding concert in Argentina's centre

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert, as at the BBC Proms

indicators.note: centre says only the middle letters of the country's name are used

explanation.surface: An exceptional concert held in the heart of Argentina.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre' takes the middle letters ENT of Argentina.
explanation.definitionFit: Prominent means standing out, conspicuous or eminent, as something outstanding does.

clue.text: Metal rod for hand-to-hand combat?

definitions.meaning: an iron bar for stirring a coal fire
a card game where players' hands of cards fight it out, with a pun on fighting at close quarters

explanation.surface: A weapon suggested for close-quarters fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: A poker stirs the fire, and poker is the card game where players pit their hands against each other.

clue.text: Bird embracing hawk-headed god's attribute

indicators.note: embracing says the bird's name wraps round the god's name

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
Ra is the Egyptian sun god, shown with a falcon's head

explanation.surface: A bird clutching a feature belonging to an Egyptian deity.
explanation.definitionFit: A trait is a distinguishing quality or characteristic, an attribute.

clue.text: Passage your compiler will read aloud

indicators.note: read aloud says the words are taken by their sound, not spelling

parts.note: your compiler means the setter, I, so the phrase becomes I'll

explanation.surface: The setter offers to recite a passage.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a walkway between rows of seats, as in a church or theatre.

clue.text: God wants Noah initially into his Ark at sea

indicators.note: into says the initial goes inside the scrambled letters
at sea means confused or adrift, so these letters are scrambled
initially picks just the first letter of the name

explanation.surface: God wants Noah to lead his creatures into the Ark while it floats on the flood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges HIS ARK, and Noah's initial N goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Krishna is a major Hindu deity, an incarnation of Vishnu.

clue.text: Stops home being covered in sticky stuff

indicators.note: being covered in says the word for home is wrapped by the sticky stuff

parts.note: resin is a sticky substance from trees
in means at home

explanation.surface: A person stays home because they're coated in something tacky.
explanation.definitionFit: To rein in is to restrain or check, as pulling a horse's reins halts it.

clue.text: Teacher in rush changed tune?

indicators.note: in says the teacher goes inside the plant word

parts.note: a rush is a reed-like waterside plant
a master is a schoolteacher

explanation.surface: A teacher in a hurry who suddenly changes their opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed tune' looks like a change of mind; here a recording is re-engineered.
explanation.definitionFit: A remastered recording has had its sound improved from the original master tape.

clue.text: Victorious time without end in sacred text

indicators.note: without end says the final letter is dropped

parts.note: VE Day, Victory in Europe Day, 8 May 1945

explanation.surface: A text about a time of triumph that never ends.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vedas are the oldest Hindu scriptures, sacred hymns written in Sanskrit.
